source: NLSY79 (U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics), respondents born 1957-1964, baseline waves 2000-2020, followed to 2022
target: Annual legal-divorce rate per person-year among intact co-resident opposite-sex married couples (Poisson rate, not a probability)

ood.method: squared Mahalanobis distance on the couple inputs (survey wave and missing flags excluded); percentile against held-out couple-intervals (the 5 committed respondent folds)
ood.unit: couple-interval (one row per respondent per baseline wave)

population_reference.method: Held-out (5 respondent folds, the committed ml_couples folds) predicted annual legal-divorce rate from the Additive enriched model for every couple-interval, survey-weighted (baseline-wave weight) quantiles; cells with fewer than 100 unweighted intervals are not published; Unknown levels omitted. p10_constant_rate is 1 - exp(-10 x rate), a 10-year projection that holds the rate fixed (the models do not project marriage length or age forward). Rows are couple-years at ages 35-64 in 2000-2022, not weddings. Held-out predictions come from re-deriving ml_couples from the public NLSY79 release (identical 40,818-interval sample and folds; held-out gains within 0.0028 percentage points of the committed ones).
